mainEntity.name: How does pricing work for electrical troubleshooting in McLean, VA?

acceptedAnswer.text: We come to the house, look at the actual work, and give a written estimate before any repair starts. Diagnostic visits include most minor on-the-spot repairs. Major repairs get a separate written estimate. No charge for the diagnostic visit in our primary service area.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you come out for a troubleshooting call in McLean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Same-day or next-day in most cases during weekday business hours. McLean is about 12 miles from our Fairfax Blvd office — roughly 22 minutes without traffic. If your situation is urgent — burning smell, sparking, warm walls — we will triage you to the earliest available slot and tell you what to shut off in the meantime.

mainEntity.name: What is included in a troubleshooting visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A real diagnostic — not a guess. We use a multimeter, circuit tracer, AFCI/GFCI tester, and IR thermal camera if heat is suspected. We open panels, test circuits at rest and under load, trace the fault to its source, then explain what we found in plain English before any repair starts.

mainEntity.name: When should I call an electrician versus trying to fix it myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call an electrician if you smell burning, see sparking, feel warm walls or warm switch plates, have a breaker that trips daily, or have lost power to part of the house without a clear cause. Resetting a tripped breaker once is fine. Resetting it three times in a row is a fire risk.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common electrical problem in McLean homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Breaker trips on overloaded circuits. McLean's median home was built in 1982, but the 22101 ZIP (central and eastern McLean — Chesterbrook, Bryn Mawr, El Nido, Langley Forest) has housing stock from the 1950s with original 100-amp panels and circuits sized for a toaster and a window AC unit. Add an induction range, central AC, a home office, and an EV charger, and those circuits can't keep up. The second most common call is flickering lights — usually a loose neutral at the meter base or a voltage drop from an aging overhead Dominion Energy service connection.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle EV charger problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. EV charging puts continuous high-amp draw on circuits that McLean's larger homes were not wired for. If your charger throttles, trips a breaker, or warms the outlet, the cause is almost always upstream — a feeder, a breaker, or a connection that cannot sustain the load. We diagnose the cause and either repair it or quote you for the right circuit.
